answer: Reputation is a scarce, unforgeable resource earned by consistently passing originality checks, and the economy spends it to filter out Sybil clusters before they can compound into a majority. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consider a hollow as the anchor of the cost. A quartz stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a jade hold...
